items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose we want to find all of the values of [MATH: x] that satisfy both [MATH: 3x+9 \geq 0] and [MATH: 2x \leq -2] simultaneously.

Content:
To do this, we solve each inequality individually and then compute the intersection of the two solutions.

Content:
- We start by solving [MATH: 3x + 9 \geq 0\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: 3x + 9|≥ 0; 3x + 9 − 9|≥ 0 − 9; 3x|≥ − 9; (3x)/(3)|≥ (− 9)/(3); x|≥ − 3]
The solution to this inequality is shown on the number line below.

[IMG: /graphics/30920650a46bfc93ee5e011c8efd5984]

Content:
- Then, we solve [MATH: 2x \leq -2\mathbin{:}]
[MATH: 2x|≤ − 2; (2x)/(2)|≤ (− 2)/(2); x|≤ − 1]
The solution to this inequality is shown on the number line below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cbd11e3c7e4794d3e255b7956ac308f7]

Content:
To find the values of [MATH: x] that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/52f64062ce2e596fecab5cf9954b9b59]

Content:
Thus, the final solution is [MATH: \color{blue}-3 \leq x \leq -1.]

To find the values of [MATH: x] that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

Thus, the final solution is [MATH: x < -2.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of [MATH: x] that satisfy both [MATH: 2-7x \geq 2] and [MATH: 10x-3 \geq 7] simultaneously.

  • First, we solve [MATH: 2-7x \geq 2\mathbin{:}] [MATH: 2 − 7x|≥ 2; 2 − 7x − 2|≥ 2 − 2; − 7x|≥ 0; (− 1) ⋅ (− 7x)|≤ (− 1) ⋅ 0; 7x|≤ 0; (7x)/(7)|≤ (0)/(7); x|≤ 0]

  • Then, we solve [MATH: 10x-3 \geq 7\mathbin{:}] [MATH: 10x − 3|≥ 7; 10x − 3 + 3|≥ 7 + 3; 10x|≥ 10; (10x)/(10)|≥ (10)/(10); x|≥ 1]

To find the values of [MATH: x] that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

It turns out that the solutions do not overlap at all. Therefore, no values of [MATH: x] satisfy both inequalities simultaneously. So, there is no solution.
